en.html:
—That connected.

From my low stance, the sword swept into his leg above the knee. Caught. Bit.
A deep gash opened in the armor.

The leg had not come off, but the force should have gone right through to the bone. His movement would certainly suffer. If stepping in became difficult, his cuts would also lose force.

A substantial advantage. Finally, something on my side.

――手応えあった。

　低い姿勢から薙ぎ払った太刀は、敵騎の膝上辺りを
とらえ、食い付き……
　浅からぬ裂傷を甲鉄に刻んでいる。

　片脚を断つまでには至らなかったが、骨に響く程の
打撃は与えた筈だ。

en.html:
Who had the advantage was clear. He could hardly fail to understand it.

All that temper, yes, but in battle Shishiku Ootori seemed to keep his judgment cold. Then if I tried speaking now, perhaps the hot blood could sit down for a moment and let him decide...?

Worth trying, at least. A fight that could be avoided, I would rather avoid.

　なら――今、改めて対話に臨めば、血気を抑えての

en.html:
Right, left. His trembling legs pulled him from side to side. Confusion inside also, it seemed.

Openings everywhere, and I deliberately did not strike. Naturally, this generosity did not extend to lowering my sword. The point stayed ready and threatening.

Give this aggressive commander one opening, and injured or not, he would cut at me. That much I did not doubt.

右へ、左へ――震える足に引き摺られて、獅子吼の
身体が揺れ動く。
　それは彼の内心の動揺を示しているとも思えた。

　隙だらけの格好に、あえて打ち込みを控える。
　だが勿論、刃先に威圧を込めて太刀を構えておくの
は忘れない。

　こちらが隙を見せれば、この気鋭の将の事、負傷を
押してでも斬り掛かって来るに相違なかった。

en.html:
Side guard. Point facing behind him. From that seated position, one step forward would let him sweep across horizontally. But—

Achha. Ready to counter, while giving the leg a rest.

Rest would help the wound heal faster. And how far it had healed, I could not observe. Standing up, his posture would tell me. Sitting without using the leg? Nothing to read.

Under pressure also, such presence of mind. Admirable. ...Whether it would do him any good, however, was still for me to decide.

Perhaps proposing a truce in the middle of a sword fight was an unbecoming weakness. Fine. But from there to assuming I would stand here while he recovered? That is taking the generosity a little far. I did not consider myself quite that sweet.

ja.html:
切先を後方に向けた、脇構えに取っている。
　座位から一歩を踏み出し、横一文字に切り払う体勢
だ――が。

　そうか。
　反撃の用意と同時に、足の負傷の回復をも試みる肚
か。

　こうして足を休ませておけば、傷の治癒も早くなる。
　しかも、その回復状況を俺の観察眼から隠蔽できる。
立っていれば姿勢の変化で察せられるが、足を使わず
座っていては看破のしようがない。

　窮地にあってこの機転、賞賛に値する。
　……だが。その機転が意味を持つかどうかは、俺の
判断に依存する事だ。

　<ruby>太刀合<rt>たちあわせ</rt></ruby>の最中に休戦提案など、たしかに武人として
あるまじき惰弱な振舞いであったかもしれないが、と
いって敵の回復を黙って許すとまで<ruby>見縊<rt>みくび</rt></ruby>られては困る。
　そこまで甘くはないつもりだ。

en.html:
In his fury, Shishiku Ootori was no different from before the armoring. Only the appearance had changed.
Sasagawa Kubo. Lieutenant General of Rokuhara. The shogunate's last great commander.

A hundred thousand Sasagawa troops under his hand. The renowned general who had defeated even Yoritsuna Okabe, Danjou-no-in—

And yet.
Something here was not fitting. By now, the mismatch was too large to ignore.

Kageaki"A sword that bewilders the eye. A feigned severe injury. Then sleight of foot with a short sword."
Kageaki"One such move, fine. An emergency reserve, some hidden technique. That I could understand. But... three."
Kageaki"Lieutenant General, you are—"
Shishiku"Tongue under control. Minato, or whatever you call yourself..."
Kageaki"............"
Shishiku"...Yes. Originally... that is what I was."
Shishiku"Not one complaint I had about my place. For Lord Tokiharu—the Ootori lord before the last—I was ready to take any filth upon this body."
Shishiku"Then that bewakoof of a last lord destroyed EVERYTHING! My proper role, gone because of him! And to carry out Lord Tokiharu's final wishes, what was left for me? The insolence of standing in HIS place!"
Shishiku"You will not understand. In the shadows I belonged, and out into the open I had to come! Into my own lord's office—the lord I had sworn to serve! This humiliation! This degradation of myself! This filth upon myself!"
Kageaki"............"
Shishiku"Laugh, then! Haan, exactly! You have understood so cleverly, no? This man they honor as Lieutenant General of Sasagawa is—¦only a creature of shadow like THIS!"

en.html:
Something terribly cold settled in my stomach. Once, I shivered.

I looked again, calmly. He seemed to have advanced half a step. That itself was no problem; there was still room between us. Something else had frightened me.

I could not tell at once.

He came closer, and first I had to inspect it. Actual movement, or my eyes playing tricks? That little delay—however I considered it, fatal.

An immediate response was impossible. He could step into cutting range and I would not know. Then he could strike, and a counterattack? Forget that. Even a defense would not be ready.

From this arrangement, how was victory supposed to come?

腹の底に酷く寒いものを覚え、一度だけ震える。

　沈静して見直せば、敵手は半歩、近付いてきたよう
だと知れた。
　それ自体はいい。まだ間合のゆとりはある。震えた
のは、別の理解のためだった。

　<ruby>咄嗟に判別がつかない<rt>・・・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>。

　対手が接近してきても、即時、それを知る事ができ
ない。錯覚か否か、検分する手間を要する。
　……どう考えても、これは致命的であった。

　敵の挙動に対する即応が不可能なのである。
　篠川公方が斬り間に踏み入ってきても、俺は察知し
得ない。そのまま彼が斬りつけてきても、反撃どころ
か防備さえ整えられない。……そうなる。

　これで勝てる道理がなかった。

The Ending stroke. Electromagnetic sword draw. Railgun.

The mechanism was exactly what the name said. Magnetic acceleration carried the stroke beyond the speed of sound, making every defense useless. No one could read it. Nothing could withstand it.

A killing technique. Not for use on a man I must not kill. Fortunately, we were on the ground. Unlike an aerial exchange at extreme speed, here I could direct the blow away from the chest, the head—the fatal places.

A severe wound, yes. But a warrior could probably heal that.

Only, one problem...

en.html:
Fundamentally, not one thing had changed.

Call my electromagnetic draw invincible. Very good. What did that actually mean? In a race of sword speed under equal conditions, I would always win. Equal conditions. Same starting line. That part was compulsory.

Were we standing on that line now? Of course not. He could detect a change in our distance before I could.

Whether he stepped in or I rushed forward, once we reached one-step cutting range, he alone would know immediately. I had to make sense of that outline first. Late, certainly.

With that difference, my godlike draw could keep sleeping in its scabbard. No opportunity to use it, and I would die under his blade. Such an excellent technique I would die holding.

So. Unless I removed this basic disadvantage, defeating Shishiku Ootori was not possible. To use the draw that guaranteed victory on equal terms, first I needed equal terms.

How?

Meaning—how to get his position. That was the whole matter.
Which of my senses could supply the information?

Eyes? They were barely bringing me that uncertain outline. What more work could I squeeze out of them?

Ears, then... how much faith could I put there? Such an overwhelming advantage, and still he was not rushing me. Surely he was keeping his footsteps silent. Sound could turn the situation around; he understood that and was guarding against it.

Read his breathing, perhaps?
Breath tells of advance and retreat. ...But this particular man might even falsify his breathing. Too much expertise in ambush and surprise. Everything he had learned, apparently, was to make my life difficult.

ja.html:
根本的に、状況は<ruby>何も<rt>・・</rt></ruby>変わっていないという点だ。

　我が電磁抜刀に無敵の二字を冠せられるとしても、
それは『互角の条件で剣速比べをしたら必ず勝つ』と
いう程度の意味に過ぎない。
　互角の条件、要は同じ<ruby>開始線<rt>スタートライン</rt></ruby>に立つ前提で必勝。

　現況がそうかと問えば、無論違った。
　対手は今、間合の変化を俺に優先して察知する権利
を所有している。

　敵の前進によってあるいは俺の突出によって、互い
の距離が<ruby>一足一刀<rt>クロスレンジ</rt></ruby>まで至った時、敵側のみがその事実
を直ちに知るのだ。
　敵像の看取に時間を要するこちらは確実に遅れる。

　この格差があっては、神速の抜刀も鞘の中で眠りに
つくほかない。
　剣技を繰り出す暇に恵まれず、俺は斬死するだろう。

　……従って。
　大鳥獅子吼に対する勝利は、この根本的劣勢を取り
除かずして実現しない。

　<ruby>五分<rt>イーブン</rt></ruby>の対決において必勝手である電磁抜刀を生かす
ため、まず条件を五分に持ち込む手筈が必要なのだ。

　如何にすべきか。

　つまり――
　如何にして敵騎の<ruby>位置情報<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>を掴むか。これに尽きる。

　俺の知覚、感覚を、どう活用すれば必要情報を得ら
れるのだろう？

　視覚か。
　……敵影をかくもあやふやな像でしか捉えられない
我が眼を、これ以上どう酷使のしようがあるのだろう。

　では聴覚……これとてどこまで当てになるか。
　圧倒的な優位にも拘わらず敵が一息に押して来ない
のは、足音を殺すために決まっている。音こそ逆転の
糸口たると彼はわきまえ、強く警戒しているのだ。

　ならば、呼吸でも読んでみるか。
　……呼吸は進退を如実に語る。だがこの男に限って
は、呼吸すら偽装しかねない。闇討奇襲の手管に長け
過ぎている。

en.html:
Against my skin I felt the moment tightening. Soon... it would be time. Doubts could remain. The decision could not. Stand here thinking and thinking—that was only another way to get myself killed. If I meant to live and complete my purpose, some other choice was required. Then decide. In this situation... which sense could I rely on?
Choices
  • Sight.
  • Hearing.
  • The sixth sense.
